item.dc:creator: Moritz Janning, Roman Kramer, Aya Abouelela, Michael Turaev, Johann Kroha, Sayak Ray

item.title: Efficient construction and explicit dimensionality of Lie group-equivariant and permutation-invariant spaces
item.description: arXiv:2604.01975v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a practical construction of functions of $N$ variables that are simultaneously equivariant under a group action and invariant under permutations, or simply group-equivariant, valid for any finite-dimensional space stable under that action. The method applies to any connected linear Lie group: it uses the Lie algebra to build a matrix $M$ whose kernel corresponds exactly to the subspace with the desired symmetry properties, removing the need for Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and explicit symmetrization over permutations. For the groups $SO(3)$ and $SU(2)$, the special structure of the matrix $M$ yields a linear scaling method which significantly outperforms the typically exponential cost of existing methods in the literature. As a byproduct, we obtain the exact dimension of group-equivariant and permutation-invariant spaces. This allows us to compare dimensionalities and show that, for large $N$, this dimension is of comparable order to that of the permutation-invariant space alone, while pre-asymptotically it is orders of magnitude lower. Enforcing group-equivariance explicitly, on top of permutation-invariance, therefore yields a substantial computational gain when approximating such functions.
item.dc:creator: Elo\"ise Barthelemy, Genevi\`eve Dusson, Camille Hernandez, Liwei Zhang

item.title: Singlet-only always-on gapless exchange (SAGE) spin qubits: Charge noise effects and two-qubit gates
item.description: arXiv:2604.15419v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Singlet-only always-on gapless exchange (SAGE) spin qubits are an alternative type of exchange-only (EO) qubits that encode a single qubit in the spins of four electrons located in four tunnel-coupled quantum dots. While conventional EO qubits are susceptible to local magnetic field gradients caused by local nuclear environments and $g$-factor variations, the SAGE qubit subspace is inherently protected from magnetic-gradient-induced Pauli errors by virtue of the singlet-only encoding, which is invariant under magnetic field gradients, and the always-on exchange couplings, which provide energetic leakage protection. However, the always-on operation simultaneously increases the qubit's sensitivity to charge noise. Here, starting from a Hubbard model describing the underlying electronic structure of the coupled quantum dots, we characterize the performance of SAGE qubits in the presence of $1/f$ charge noise that induces fluctuations in both the dot chemical potentials and the interdot tunnel couplings. We calculate SAGE idle coherence times and show that realistic CPMG-like pulse sequences can be used to significantly extend SAGE single-qubit coherence times for experimentally relevant charge noise strengths. We likewise study the fidelity of SAGE two-qubit gates in the presence of charge and magnetic noise and again propose a simple refocusing strategy to mitigate the noise, while increased ramp times of the entangling pulse suppress leakage into noncomputational states.
item.dc:creator: Nathan L. Foulk, Katharina Laubscher, Silas Hoffman, Sankar Das Sarma

item.title: Ising anyons in the $SU(2)_2$ Chern--Simons theory
item.description: arXiv:2605.15268v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ising anyons and $SU(2)_2$ Chern--Simons theory share the fusion rules and $F$-symbols, and their $R$-symbols agree up to braiding orientation and an overall phase. The quantum-group description, $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at $q = e^{i\pi/4}$, is nevertheless not semisimple: tensor powers of the fundamental representation contain an additional spin-$3/2$ representation and reducible indecomposable representations, all of zero quantum dimension. We construct explicit highest-weight bases for up to four strands, compute the Racah and braiding matrices, and show that for four strands changes of fusion basis and braiding mix the physical sector with an indecomposable summand. We prove that this mixing affects neither the braid-closure invariant nor the plat-closure amplitude for any number of strands, so that each braiding matrix can be replaced by its physical block. The full representation theory thus reproduces the Ising-anyon data for all observables relevant to topological quantum computation.
item.dc:creator: Artem Belov, Andrey Morozov

item.title: Topological metal-insulator transitions in one-dimensional non-Hermitian quasicrystals: beyond PT-symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2605.25072v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: One-dimensional non-Hermitian quasicrystals with parity and time-reversal (PT) symmetry can simultaneously exhibit localization-delocalization transition, topological phase transition, and PT-symmetry-breaking transition. This motivates us to investigate how the absence of PT symmetry impacts topological metal-insulator transitions in non-Hermitian quasicrystals. We propose a non-Hermitian quasiperiodic model that generally does not preserve PT-symmetry but, in most parameter regions, hosts a generic triple-transition scenario encompassing localization, topological, and degeneracy-breaking transitions. These transitions can be understood within the dual momentum-space representation featuring asymmetric couplings. Specifically, the localization boundary is obtained from the dual momentum-space representation by comparing the Lyapunov exponent, or inverse localization length, of the reciprocal Aubry-Andr\'e model with the nonreciprocal hopping-asymmetry ratio of the dual lattice. The accompanying topological transition is characterized by a point-gap winding number defined with respect to a reference energy inside the complex spectral gap, whereas the degeneracy-breaking transition is understood from the loss of the reciprocal $n\leftrightarrow -n$ spectral symmetry. The system also exhibits a localization-delocalization transition analogous to that in the Hermitian case, which occurs without accompanying topological or degeneracy-breaking transitions. Our work extends the topological metal-insulator transitions previously studied in PT-symmetric systems to a more general class of non-Hermitian setting, and further reveals that non-Hermitian systems can host distinct types of localization behavior.
item.dc:creator: Guangjie Zhang, Bing Shao, Longwen Zhou, Jiangbin Gong, Weiwei Zhu

item.title: Entanglement in Presence of Topological Interfaces and Dualities
item.description: arXiv:2607.22451v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Entanglement through interfaces has attracted considerable attention in 2d conformal field theory (CFT). However, it is known that field-theoretic predictions based on the existing framework are in general incompatible with numerical results [1-4]. A new framework for entanglement through topological defects was recently proposed in [5]. It provides a general description of entanglement through topological defects and successfully reproduces the numerical results for the Ising model in all tested cases and regimes. The key insight is that the relevant quantum correlations are encoded in twisted states, allowing for the construction of the full reduced density matrix (RDM). In this work we pursue two objectives. First, we provide new examples by studying defects in the free boson CFT. Second, we extend the framework to topological interfaces connecting two, possibly distinct, CFTs. Of particular interest are interfaces relating dual theories. We show that the reduced density matrix for a duality interface is the projection of the vacuum reduced density matrix onto a single symmetry sector, closely paralleling the framework of symmetry resolution. Unlike symmetry resolution, however, the projection is imposed by the physical interface itself, demonstrating that duality interfaces reflect quantum correlations back into the entangling interval. We establish this mechanism for diagonal and non-diagonal rational CFTs as well as the free boson CFT. Relative entropy allows us to quantify the distinguishability of the duality interface RDM from the vacuum RDM.
item.dc:creator: Christian Northe, Riccardo Poletti, Paolo Rossi

item.title: GPU implementation of mixed quantum-classical Liouville molecular dynamics without momentum jump
item.description: arXiv:2608.14544v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We implemented on GPU a mixed quantum-classical Liouville molecular dynamics simulation based on a momentum-jump-free theory. The trajectory spawning that was previously implemented on CPU for sampling enhancement was eliminated to avoid the overhead of thread divergence and dynamic memory allocation on the GPU. The method was applied to a three-dimensional spin-boson model and a three-mode model of $S_2 \to S_1$ internal conversion in pyrazine involving a conical intersection. A speedup of an order of magnitude compared to the CPU computation with spawning was achieved, as well as a linear scaling with respect to the number of sampling trajectories.
item.dc:creator: Koji Ando

item.title: Transport-Noise and Optical Witnesses of Electronic Multipartite Entanglement
item.description: arXiv:2608.16028v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Entanglement among particles distinguishes correlated quantum materials from conventional metals and semiconductors. Experimentally certifying intrinsic entanglement among interacting electrons in materials is important not only for classifying states of matter, but also for developing material-based quantum technologies. Here, we introduce a transport protocol for witnessing multipartite entanglement from the equilibrium current-noise spectrum, measured directly or reconstructed from optical conductivity. The appropriately integrated, symmetrized, and projected noise spectrum obeys an upper bound derived from microscopic model parameters. Unlike witnesses based on localized spins, our framework applies to general electronic states without requiring magnetic moments and remains invariant under single-particle basis transformations. We benchmark it in twisted bilayer graphene, twisted bilayer MoTe$_2$, and Hubbard models, and demonstrate entanglement certification in a fractional Chern insulator. This approach extends recently developed scattering-based entanglement witnesses to ultralow-temperature conditions, where many candidate entangled phases emerge.
item.dc:creator: Shuhan Ding, Prakash Sharma, Zecheng Shen, Jiang-Xiazi Lin, Sergei Urazhdin, Yao Wang

item.title: Massive quantum divergence on the Cauchy horizon of a black hole
item.description: arXiv:2609.10755v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate a quantum {\it massive} scalar field in the interior of a charged and spherically-symmetric (Reissner-Nordstr\"om) black hole. We examine the behaviour for varying values of the black hole charge, field mass and coupling constant when the field is in two quantum states: Hartle-Hawking (representing a black hole in thermal equilibrium) and Unruh (representing a black hole evaporating via the emission of Hawking radiation). We show that the vacuum polarization (in both states) generically {\it diverges} on the Cauchy horizon, in stark contrast to what happens for massless fields; also, the angular components of the quantum stress-energy tensor generically {\it diverge} on the Cauchy horizon and, in at least one of the two states, they do so more strongly than for massless fields. Furthermore, we calculate the energy fluxes in Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates $\{u,v\}$. We show that these fluxes in both states on the Cauchy horizon do not generically vanish. This implies, in particular, that in regular, Kruskal coordinates $\{U,V\}$ the ingoing flux diverges like $V^{-2}$ on the Cauchy horizon (where $V=0$). This divergence suggests that its backreaction via the semiclassical Einstein equations would yield a strong singularity, as opposed to its weaker, classical counterpart. Interestingly, there are exceptions, in which the energy fluxes in Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates vanish: (i) in the extremal limit (where the black hole is maximally charged); (ii) certain fine-tuned regions of parameter space, where the fluxes change sign.
item.dc:creator: Marc Casals, Lorenzo Pisani, Peter Taylor

item.title: Multicomponent anyons in one-dimensional optical lattices
item.description: arXiv:2609.36554v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the ground-state and dynamical properties of multicomponent interacting anyons confined in a one-dimensional (1D) optical lattice. Adopting the Anyon-Hubbard model, we explore spin and charge correlations as functions of interaction strength and the anyonic statistical parameter. Our results demonstrate that multicomponent effects combined with fractional exchange statistics substantially reshape both charge and spin correlations. For fractional exchange statistics, the canonical symmetric shell structure with prominent singularities in the spinor fermionic momentum distribution undergoes notable structural reconstruction, exhibiting emergent asymmetry, new spectral peaks, and broadened singular features. Unlike the Tonks-Girardeau bosonic gas, pseudobosons, representing a limiting case of anyons, cease to display a dominant zero-momentum peak. Instead, a quasi-fermionic shell structure emerges with finite-momentum peaks, whose locations are modulated by lattice site occupancy and interaction strength. The structure factor of spin correlations uncovers antiferromagnetic ordering in spinor anyon systems, with correlation magnitudes tunable by anyonic exchange statistics. Furthermore, quench dynamics analysis reveals the statistical phase parameter as an effective tuning knob. It enables the switching of dipole oscillations between underdamped and overdamped relaxation regimes and governs overall cloud expansion dynamics. Our findings pave the way for exploring statistics-driven ground-state and dynamical phase transitions in spinor anyon systems.
item.dc:creator: Sagarika Basak, Xi-Wen Guan, Han Pu

item.title: Generalized Effective Spin-Chain formalism for multicomponent anyons in one-dimensional optical lattices
item.description: arXiv:2609.36555v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a generalized effective spin-chain (GESC) formalism for strongly interacting multicomponent anyons in a one-dimensional (1D) optical lattice. By mapping particle motion onto spinless fermions and spin states onto an ordered chain, this framework provides a spin-charge-separated perspective on the physical effects of fractional exchange statistics. In the strong-interaction regime, the leading-order charge Hamiltonian becomes independent of the statistical phase; instead, virtual tunneling through doubly occupied states directly imprints this phase on the spin-exchange coefficients. The GESC formalism captures ground-state properties of the full Anyon-Hubbard model reported in S.~Basak, X.-W.~Guan, and H.~Pu, unpublished manuscript (2026), and reveals that their statistical dependence is predominantly encoded in the explicit anyonic structure of the observables rather than the underlying spin ground state. This formalism uncovers that, out of equilibrium, successive spin exchanges accumulate direction-dependent phases; the resulting interference drives crossover from dispersive to localized impurity transport and generates inversion-asymmetric propagation at intermediate statistics. Suppressed expansion persists for identical and distinguishable impurities, with differences in propagation governed by the interplay between impurity identity and interaction anisotropy. Ultimately, GESC offers a versatile, computationally efficient theoretical framework that connects macroscopic dynamics to microscopic virtual exchange processes, conferring a unique spin-charge-separated vantage for resolving how fractional exchange statistics survives strong interactions and manifests distinctly across static and dynamical regimes.
item.dc:creator: Sagarika Basak, Xi-Wen Guan, Han Pu

item.title: The Puzzle of the Replica Transition at Ising Criticality
item.description: arXiv:2610.13802v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Critical quantum ground states exhibit universal properties governed by conformal field theories (CFTs), yet some of these universal signatures remain poorly understood even for the paradigmatic Ising chain in 1+1d at its quantum critical point. In particular, numerical studies have long identified universal contributions to its ground-state measurement statistics, but their origin remains unexplained. Replica methods offer a natural framework to study such post-measurement statistics, with the replica limit $Q\to 1$ describing the physical Born-averaged ensemble. Here we show that, for the monitored critical Ising chain, the replicated post-measurement ensemble of states itself undergoes a phase transition precisely at the physically relevant replica limit $Q \to 1$, preventing standard replica treatments. We use boundary conformal field theory (BCFT) methods to explain the underlying mechanism of this transition. Our methods yield a perturbative analytic calculation of the universal O(1) constant in the Shannon entropy of the measurement record, previously known only numerically. We also apply our tools to study measurement-averaged spin correlators, providing a unified description of the universal properties of measurement outcomes and post-measurement states.
item.dc:creator: Kabir Khanna, Sara Murciano, Romain Vasseur

item.title: Nonperturbative optomechanics with thin, weakly reflective intracavity dielectrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.15749v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Levitated dielectric sensors are often treated as perturbative probes of a pre-existing optical field. We show that this picture fails for a novel sensor geometry: a dielectric plate whose transverse extent captures the full optical mode. Even an optically thin sensor with modest refractive index can heavily restructure the intracavity fields, effectively partitioning a cavity into two subcavities with substantial cross-coupling and producing new optical resonances and trapping sites with properties which deviate from the standard intuition. Conventional perturbative expressions for the cavity frequency shift and optomechanical coupling depart from the exact solution at thicknesses as small as $\sim\lambda/(10n)$. Furthermore, cavity locking decreases the coupling and increases the trap stiffness by orders of magnitude, and the coupled subcavity structure permits appreciable optical cooling at zero detuning, a distinct behavior unique to this nonperturbative regime. These effects, sharing a common origin, establish a distinct regime of cavity optomechanics in which the sensor is no longer merely a probe of the cavity field, but an element that helps define it.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Laeuger, Nancy Aggarwal

item.title: Vectorized and Symbolically Optimized Seminumerical Exchange for Large-Scale Quantum Chemistry
item.description: arXiv:2610.21075v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a seminumerical exchange algorithm (SNK) based on the sn-LinK method [Laqua et al., J. Chem. Theory Comput. 16, 1456 (2020)], optimized for modern multi-core central processing units with single instruction multiple data vector instructions and report its implementation into the Q-Chem quantum chemistry program. Vectorization and memory management strategies for the Boys function and 3-center-1-electron (3c1e) integral kernels are given. Several new considerations are made in the computation of the 3c1e integrals: the Head-Gordon Pople horizontal recurrence relations, same-center optimizations, and multishell optimizations, all implemented symbolically employing the SymPy symbolic algebra library and exported as optimized C++ code leveraging common-sub-expression elimination (CSE) optimization techniques. A general scheme for choosing optimal integral kernels is developed through rigorous timing benchmarks. The resulting implementation is tested against traditional 4c2e exchange for several systems and basis sets, showing 1-2 orders of magnitude speedups for systems of practically relevant sizes (100-500 atoms, 2000-10000 basis functions). For smaller molecules, comparisons are also made against the more efficient occ-RI-K method showing a break-even point around 50-100 atoms beyond which SNK dramatically outperforms due to its superior sub-quadratic (between linear and quadratic) time complexity as well as its effectively negligible memory demand.
item.dc:creator: Jesse DiCenso, Henryk Laqua, Martin Head-Gordon

item.title: Minimal-length kinematics of coherent light and a proposed two-color vacuum chronoscopy
item.description: arXiv:2610.26892v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The unification of quantum theory and general relativity suggests the existence of a minimal measurable length, leading to a generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) and an energy-dependent vacuum group velocity. Testing these effects with macroscopic objects typically encounters the ``soccer-ball problem,'' where applying Planck-scale deformations to the total momentum predicts observationally ruled-out velocity deviations. We adopt the prescription, natural in quantum field theory (QFT), in which the GUP modifies single-mode commutators, and verify by explicit calculation that the macroscopic group velocity of a multimode coherent pulse reduces to the single-photon GUP velocity evaluated at the central wavelength, multiplied by the classical Gaussian-beam factor, with no dependence on the total pulse energy. The energy--momentum relation $E=pc$ itself is unmodified; the deformation enters through the velocity--momentum relation and is equivalent to a modified dispersion relation in the wave vector, with a quadratic coefficient that depends on which of the two variables is used. The soccer-ball problem --- which arises only when the GUP is applied to the center-of-mass momentum of a composite system --- is therefore absent for coherent light, and macroscopic petawatt pulses probe the same parameter space as single high-energy photons. Building on this framework, we propose a two-color vacuum chronoscopy experiment using a short-pulse petawatt laser and its high-harmonic generation. By systematically varying the macroscopic beam waist, our setup separates Planck-scale kinematic shifts from classical diffraction delays, establishing a controlled, source-independent terrestrial methodology whose sensitivity we assess against current astrophysical bounds and against the dominant waist-independent systematics that limit it, residual-gas dispersion and the harmonic birth-time offset.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Wang, Saurya Das, Samuel L. Braunstein
